title: PINES Management Processes — Reporting and Administrative Tools
scope: Reporting, analysis, batch administrative utilities and supporting infrastructure used by PINES staff, managers and administrators to manage collections, patrons, transactions and financial records across the consortium. This specification covers report content, batch item utilities, data access controls, operational constraints (OS, browsers, accessibility), and developer-provided metadata/documentation. It does not redefine OPAC patron-facing features except where reports read OPAC-created data.

glossary.definition: A saved, administrator-managed report definition that staff can run as-is or (where allowed) clone and modify.
A report run as an asynchronous job on the server or reporting subsystem that does not block interactive clients.
A batch operation that moves item records from one location to another (for pull lists, outreach, mobile libraries, temporary events, etc.).
An item or bibliographic instance that, within the chosen scope (library or system), is the only copy owned by that scope.
Online Public Access Catalog — the patron-facing web/catalog interface that creates holds and transactions which reports may read.

requirements.name: Material volume reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide reports that show the volume of material for a selected library or group of libraries at any point in time, including counts for new acquisitions, items on shelf (checked in) and items out in circulation, and allow breaking down results by category (examples: total items, holds count, adult fiction, board books). Categories shall be configurable per library and templates shall be able to expose custom categories for reuse. (Sources: DOC-001, DOC-010, DOC-015)
requirements.priority_reason: Direct stakeholder request as a key monthly/board reporting need and repeated endorsement across working-group documents.

requirements.name: System capacity interface
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a high-level interface displaying capacity and key metrics for all branches at once, with the ability to drill down to individual branch detail, sort and filter by region, library type or current load, display trend data (growth/shrink patterns), and export results to CSV for directors. The interface shall support grouping of locations where necessary to avoid overwhelming displays. (Sources: DOC-002, DOC-010, DOC-018)
requirements.priority_reason: Expressed as a system-level need for cross-branch planning and explicitly requested by multiple stakeholders.

requirements.name: Shelf-space utilization report
requirements.explanation: The system shall produce a shelf-space report, per selected library or for the system, that compares for each genre and format: percentage of total circulations, percentage of the collection, and percentage of total shelf space; the report shall support side-by-side comparison across libraries and date-range filtering. Because shelf space may not be tracked directly, the requirement allows use of calculated estimates (e.g., item dimensions or item-count proxies) and requires the report to document the estimation method used. (Sources: DOC-003, DOC-010, DOC-015)
requirements.priority_reason: Cataloging and collection managers requested this to support weeding/space decisions, and stakeholders emphasized per-branch and system views.

requirements.name: Batch item transfer utility
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a batch item transfer utility that allows staff with appropriate permissions to: build queries for candidate materials (and save those queries as templates), manually select items from query results, change selected items' location fields for transfer, generate pull/transit lists (printable), and optionally schedule or execute an automatic revert to original location based on elapsed time or event criteria. The utility shall support preview and confirmation before applying changes, an undo mechanism where feasible, printable transit labels and transfer delay alerts, and shall record transfer history for each item. Batch updates shall use transaction-safe processing and be efficient for very large collections. (Sources: DOC-004, DOC-010, DOC-015, DOC-019)
requirements.priority_reason: Multiple cataloging and branch staff identified this as critical for outreach, mobile services, and routine redistribution; technical staff noted batch/transaction safety is essential.

requirements.name: Missing, damaged and in-transit reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide two related reports: (a) missing and damaged items report by branch with optional inclusion of condition notes (e.g., 'water damage', 'vandalism') and time-range filtering for trend analysis; and (b) an in-transit items report that lists items that have been in-transit more than X days (X configurable, default suggested 7 days), merging both transit-to and transit-from perspectives and allowing sorting by due date to prioritize follow-up. Both reports shall be runnable per branch and system-wide. (Sources: DOC-005, DOC-015)
requirements.priority_reason: Front-line and delivery staff repeatedly requested both reports to manage inventory, reduce losses, and coordinate deliveries.

requirements.name: Item record purging and last-copy protection
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide reports and a safety-controlled utility to identify item records for purging using customizable criteria (status, time in status, last circulation dates, combinations of criteria), assist with batch status conversions, and provide an efficient mechanism to delete volume and copy entries and orphan bibliographic records. Critically, the system shall produce a 'last copy report' that flags items which are the last copy within a chosen scope (branch or system) so catalogers can avoid accidental deletion. Purging operations shall be driven from read-only candidate reports, require a separate explicit confirmation step, and create an audit trail recording who performed actions and when. The utility may be schedulable for recurring runs but must protect against accidental mass deletion. (Sources: DOC-006, DOC-015, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Cataloging and collection staff defined this as critical (last-copy protection named 'CRITICAL'), and stakeholders required safety/audit controls.

requirements.name: Deletion-audit and deletion reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall log all successful and attempted (denied) deletions of records (item, patron, bibliographic) to an audit table via database triggers or equivalent, capturing record type, record identifier, user who attempted the deletion, timestamp, and the operator's location; a report interface shall enable aggregation of deletions by period, by user, by location and by type for auditing and compliance. (Sources: DOC-007, DOC-010, DOC-019)
requirements.priority_reason: Stakeholders require traceability for accountability and compliance; technical staff indicated database triggers are feasible and necessary.

requirements.name: Patron characteristics and demographic queries
requirements.explanation: The system shall support limiting and grouping queries and reports by patron characteristics including configurable age ranges, zip code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language; it must support combined filters with AND/OR logic and include records with null/missing values rather than implicitly excluding them. (Sources: DOC-008, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Program planners and outreach staff explicitly requested these filters and groupings for program targeting; configurability and inclusion of nulls were emphasized.

requirements.name: Inactive patrons reporting and outreach export
requirements.explanation: The system shall generate lists of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity in the last X days, where X is configurable (supporting at least 30, 90, 180, 365 and arbitrary values) and the report can be scoped to System, Home Library, County or other levels. The report shall optionally include current mailing addresses, flag or separate patrons with outstanding fines, allow exclusion rules (do-not-disturb, VIPs, staff, opt-outs), be exportable to CSV and be runnable as a background job for large patron sets. (Sources: DOC-009, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Multiple libraries run these reports routinely for database cleanup and outreach; performance concerns require background processing.

requirements.name: Operating environment and scalability
requirements.explanation: The system shall support a consortium-scale environment (example scale: 286 locations, ~17M annual circulations, large acquisition volumes), operate on Linux or Solaris servers, be usable via web-browser or Windows client, support IE 6.0+ and Firefox 2.0+ where web-based, and ensure report processing can occur without disrupting OPAC or circulation clients (by background processing, replicas or other architectural separation). (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-016, DOC-018, DOC-019)
requirements.priority_reason: Technical constraints and scale were repeatedly called out by IT stakeholders and working-group materials.

requirements.name: Accessibility, standards and platform constraints
requirements.explanation: The system shall comply with accessibility requirements (support screen readers, screen magnification and other assistive technologies and produce standards-compliant HTML), use a fully relational database back-end, and provide development/training environments with migration capability to production. The reporting subsystem shall not constrain OPAC functionality or responsiveness. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-016, DOC-019, DOC-018)
requirements.priority_reason: Legal accessibility obligations and architectural constraints were explicitly stated by multiple stakeholders and technical staff.

requirements.name: Developer-provided data specifications, process descriptions and help
requirements.explanation: The developer shall supply comprehensive data specifications (field names, types and relationships) for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request and other records used by management reports; a high-level description of major processes (imports/exports, validation flows) and an online, hierarchical, cross-linked HTML help system. Error reporting shall include high-level and low-level, query-specific feedback for administrators. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-019, DOC-018)
requirements.priority_reason: Staff need documentation and meaningful error feedback to author and troubleshoot reports; several documents required developer-supplied specs and help.

requirements.name: Query tool and open-template reporting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a user-friendly query/report designer across all record types (bib, item, patron, transaction, financial) that supports field selection, picklists, Boolean logic (AND/OR), configurable regular-expression use where appropriate, saved queries, and an 'open template' mode exposing all attributes for filtering and display. Administrators shall be able to restrict access to tables/fields. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-012, DOC-014, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Repeated user demand for a flexible query designer and open template reporting across multiple documents and survey results.

requirements.name: Report templates, permissions and shared folders
requirements.explanation: Administrators shall be able to create, publish and manage report templates; templates must be runnable as-is, clonable for modification, and support administrator limits on which filters/display fields can be altered. The system shall support fine-grained permissions for creating, cloning and running reports, and shared folders to manage access by role, workgroup or individual. Role-assignments must be administrable so permission changes follow role changes. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-012, DOC-018, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: High priority across stakeholders for consistent board reports, controlled templates, and easy admin of permissions.

requirements.name: Report scheduling, queue visibility, prioritization and cancellation
requirements.explanation: The system shall allow reports to be scheduled (ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly), run as background jobs, show queue position and status (waiting, running, completed, failed) to requestors, allow certain reports to be prioritized to jump ahead in queue, and permit cancellation of scheduled or running reports. Administrators shall be able to configure recurring reports and their recipients. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-012, DOC-019, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Queue visibility and prioritization were repeatedly reported as operational needs to prevent user confusion and support directors' reporting needs.

requirements.name: Report output formats, delivery and export
requirements.explanation: Reports shall be exportable in CSV and HTML formats and provide reliable Excel-compatible output (or Excel export) for downstream use (pivot tables). The system shall support emailing report results to specified addresses (address book supported) and include the report selection criteria and report name in outputs. Reports shall support pivot table-capable exports and inclusion of all null/blank fields. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-011, DOC-012, DOC-019, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Export and delivery features are important for directors and integrations; they were requested frequently but are not safety-critical relative to core reporting.

requirements.name: Historical reporting and reporting warehouse
requirements.explanation: The system shall support historical reporting requirements (snapshots for given dates/date ranges). Where required for performance and reproducible historical snapshots, a reporting warehouse or other archival mechanism shall be provided to retain historical state separate from production row-level changes. The system shall indicate whether a result is from a historical snapshot or real-time data. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-019, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Users requested historical snapshots and technical staff indicated a warehouse may be required to provide this reliably without impacting production.

requirements.name: Transaction reporting and types
requirements.explanation: The system shall retain transaction history for a configurable period (transaction history retained X days configurable) while keeping monthly and annual aggregates indefinitely, and provide reports that group transactions by hour, terminal, branch and system; count types of check-in (book-drop, by terminal, by user/self-service) and check-out (staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self renewal, online renewals) individually and cumulatively; and produce transaction reports (holds placed, holds filled, check-outs) per patron, per library, per selected group, per system, or per county. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Detailed transaction counting and grouping are core reporting needs used daily by branches and managers.

requirements.name: Financial reporting and audit trail
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide financial reports including value-of-items aggregations (using purchase price fields) for an entire collection or a selected portion, patron account balances by patron/home library/system, fines and charges accrued per period and per type, fines waived per period and branch, and payments by period and payment method. The system shall maintain an auditable ledger of patron payments that records which charges payments are applied to and shall support reconciliation and compliance with applicable accounting/archival retention policies. (Sources: DOC-011, DOC-010)
requirements.priority_reason: Finance stakeholders explicitly required value and ledger capabilities and legal/audit compliance.

requirements.name: Canned, on-demand and open-template report interfaces
requirements.explanation: The system shall support three reporting interfaces: canned report templates (predefined templates runnable ASAP or scheduled), on-demand editable reports for preset categories, and open-template reporting exposing all attributes for advanced ad-hoc queries; canned reports shall be discoverable with descriptive hover pop-ups and administrators shall deliver a set of pre-written templates. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-014, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Stakeholders asked for distinct modes (canned, on-demand, open-template) to cover common and ad-hoc needs; this organizes functionality and training.

requirements.name: Uncataloged material inventory and counting
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide a minimal-labor workflow to record, distribute and count uncataloged material (e.g., paperback/children's board books) so those transactions contribute to circulation statistics and can be identified in reports while avoiding full cataloging overhead. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-015)
requirements.priority_reason: Multiple branches identified uncataloged material handling as a practical need for rapid distribution and counting.

requirements.name: Data quality and bibliographic integrity reports
requirements.explanation: The system shall provide data quality reports for identifying bibliographic and item anomalies such as bibliographic records with no volumes attached, records missing specific MARC fields, items with invalid item type or excessively long call numbers, items with zero use count or candidate weeding lists, and a mechanism to retrieve last-edit and last-circulation metadata separately. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-015, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: Cataloging staff require specialized data-quality reporting to maintain catalog integrity and support weeding decisions.

requirements.name: Authentication and role-based access control
requirements.explanation: The system shall support streamlined but optional staff login mechanisms (e.g., card-swipe) and also traditional username/password; every login must identify which staff member is logged in for auditing. User rights shall be defined and administered via roles/security groups (Staff, Local Admin, Library Manager, Global Admin) to simplify permission changes and to control report and template operations. (Sources: DOC-013, DOC-016, DOC-018)
requirements.priority_reason: Operational security, auditability and local administrative ease were emphasized repeatedly.

requirements.name: Miscellaneous quick-access and fine-grained features
requirements.explanation: The system shall support assorted usability and integration items requested repeatedly: ability to include selection criteria in outputs; upload text files (barcodes/TCNs) to filter reports; allow pivot-compatible exports; allow retrieval of MARC fields in single-row outputs; allow report result comparison columns (month-over-month, percent change); and provide an address-book for delivery recipients. (Sources: DOC-010, DOC-012, DOC-014, DOC-020)
requirements.priority_reason: These features improve day-to-day usability for report consumers and were frequently requested; they are enhancements rather than core safety items.

open_questions.question: How should 'shelf space' be calculated when no explicit shelf-space field exists?
open_questions.reason: Stakeholders require a shelf-space percentage metric but multiple sources note the database does not track shelf space directly. The specification permits estimation but the exact algorithm (item dimensions, per-format average linear inches, or item-count proxy) was not decided.

open_questions.question: What scope and definitive metric(s) define 'capacity' for the capacity interface (e.g., physical shelf linear-feet, configured item limits, circulation processing capacity)?
open_questions.reason: Participants requested a system-wide capacity dashboard but asked different questions about what 'capacity' means. Implementation requires a stakeholder decision to select concrete metrics to display.

open_questions.question: Which archival retention policy values shall the system enforce by default (e.g., transaction retention X days, financial archival years)?
open_questions.reason: Documents reference configurable retention and an example 7-year finance retention but did not lock specific defaults; this requires policy decision for defaults and guidance for configuration.

open_questions.question: For auto-revert of transferred items: which event triggers or precedence rules should be supported (time-based first, event-based overrides, checked-out at destination to cancel auto-revert)?
open_questions.reason: Stakeholders asked for both time-based and event-based auto-revert behaviors, but interactions and precedence (e.g., revert after X days unless checked out at destination) were not fully specified.

open_questions.question: Should historical reporting use a separate reporting replica with periodic snapshots, or a dedicated reporting warehouse mirroring the production schema?
open_questions.reason: Technical staff raised performance and reproducibility concerns; choice affects architecture, latency and complexity.
